title: Finite curve trace-cup products commute with reduction and semilinear isomorphisms
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $C/k$ be a smooth proper connected curve [def-sc-curves], and let $\ell$ be a prime different from $\operatorname{char}k$. For $n\geq1$ put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ and let $\mu_{\ell^n}$ be the etale sheaf of units $z$ satisfying $z^{\ell^n}=1$, as in [def-sc-kummer-sequence]. Use ordinary small-etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Write $\operatorname{tr}_{C,n}:H^2(C,\mu_{\ell^n})\to A_n$ for the canonical degree-normalized trace (the class of each closed point $P$ has trace $1$; its class means the image of $\mathcal O_C(P)$ under the Kummer connecting map, with divisor sheaves as in [def-sc-divisor]). For $i=0,1,2$, let
$$
P^i_{C,n}(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}_{C,n}(x\smile y),\qquad
x\in H^i(C,A_n),\quad y\in H^{2-i}(C,\mu_{\ell^n}),
$$
where cup product is the derived global-sections cup product followed by the coefficient evaluation $A_n\otimes\mu_{\ell^n}\to\mu_{\ell^n}$.
For $n\geq m\geq1$, let $r_{n,m}$ on untwisted cohomology be induced by $A_n\to A_m$, and let $s_{n,m}$ on twisted cohomology be induced by $z\mapsto z^{\ell^{n-m}}$. Then
$$
P^i_{C,m}(r_{n,m}x,s_{n,m}y)
= P^i_{C,n}(x,y)\bmod\ell^m.
$$
Let $D/k$ also be a smooth proper connected curve and let $f:D\to C$ be an isomorphism of schemes covering any automorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the canonical pullback identifications of the constant and roots-of-unity sheaves. Then
$$
P^i_{D,n}(f^*x,f^*y)=P^i_{C,n}(x,y).
$$
No finite-field or Frobenius hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For either curve $T=C,D$ and every $r\geq1$, write $\delta_{T,r}:\operatorname{Pic}(T)\to H^2(T,\mu_{\ell^r})$ for the Kummer boundary. By [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors] this map is surjective. By [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve], every line-bundle class is the class of $\mathcal O_T(E)$ for a divisor $E$. Since [def-sc-divisor] makes the divisor group free on closed points and the divisor-class map is additive, the elements $\delta_{T,r}(\mathcal O_T(P))$ generate $H^2(T,\mu_{\ell^r})$ as an abelian group. Thus two additive maps out of this group agree if they agree on these point classes.

source.place: Proposition 14.2 and the divisor/Picard description used in its proof

proof.text: On each of the two small etale sites, the category of abelian sheaves is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Global sections is additive and left exact: the sectionwise kernel of a sheaf morphism is a sheaf (compatible sections glue in the source and remain in the kernel), and its global sections are the kernel of the map on global sections. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], applied to global sections and the cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], says that a morphism $(a,b,c)$ of short exact sequences commutes with connecting maps: $H^{q+1}(a)\delta=\delta'H^q(c)$. These $\delta$-functor connecting maps are the ones used everywhere below: by [lem-sc-p1-right-derived-triangle-connecting], under the canonical identification $R^q\Gamma(F)\cong H^q(R\Gamma(T_{\Et},F[0]))$, which is the cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], they are the homology connecting maps of the distinguished triangle $A[0]\to B[0]\to C[0]\to A[0][1]$ of the short exact sequence after applying $R\Gamma$. These are the connecting maps of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] and the Kummer coboundaries of [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors] and of the item's trace normalization. We will use precisely this coefficient naturality, in addition to the change-of-site naturality below.

source.place: Section 01FT, cohomology-sheaves: right derived global sections are a universal delta-functor; derived.tex, Tag 015B and Tag 05TE

proof.text:
Put $d=\ell^{n-m}$. Both Kummer sequences are short exact by [lem-sc-kummer-exact], since $\ell$ is invertible in $k$. There is a morphism from the level-$n$ sequence to the level-$m$ sequence whose three nonzero vertical maps, in order, are
$$\mu_{\ell^n}\xrightarrow{z\mapsto z^d}\mu_{\ell^m},\qquad \mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{u\mapsto u^d}\mathbf G_m,\qquad \mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathbf G_m.$$
The first square commutes by inclusion, and the second because $(u^d)^{\ell^m}=u^{\ell^n}$. Connecting-map naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor], as applied in Step 2, gives
$$s_{n,m}\delta_{C,n}(L)=\delta_{C,m}(L)$$
for every $L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, using the Kummer/Picard boundary of [lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors]. In particular there is no extra factor $d$ on the line-bundle input: that input belongs to the final, identity-mapped copy of $\mathbf G_m$.

source.place: Proposition 14.2: Kummer description of H2; coefficient ladder written explicitly here, with Stacks 01FT for boundary naturality

proof.text:
Let $\rho:A_n\to A_m$ be reduction. On a point generator from Step 1, Step 3 and the given degree normalization give
$$\operatorname{tr}_{C,m}(s_{n,m}\delta_{C,n}(\mathcal O_C(P)))=1=\rho(\operatorname{tr}_{C,n}(\delta_{C,n}(\mathcal O_C(P)))).$$
Both sides are additive, so generation proves $\operatorname{tr}_{C,m}\circ s_{n,m}=\rho\circ\operatorname{tr}_{C,n}$ on all of $H^2(C,\mu_{\ell^n})$.

source.place: Proposition 14.5 and Remark 14.6: trace normalization on point classes

proof.text:
The evaluation square for $A_n,\mu_{\ell^n},\mu_{\ell^n}$ and $A_m,\mu_{\ell^m},\mu_{\ell^m}$ commutes. Indeed for an integer representative $a$ and $z^{\ell^n}=1$, $(z^a)^d=(z^d)^a=(z^d)^{a\bmod\ell^m}$, since $z^d$ has order dividing $\ell^m$. Apply [lem-wf-etale-cup-functoriality] with $f=\mathrm{id}_C$, coefficient maps $(\rho,s_{n,m},s_{n,m})$ and these evaluations. For $p=i$, $q=2-i$ this gives
$$s_{n,m}(x\smile y)=r_{n,m}x\smile s_{n,m}y.$$
All these sheaves are abelian sheaves, and evaluation is the indicated bilinear pairing over $\mathbf Z$.

For the scheme isomorphism $f:D\to C$, pullback of units gives $c_f:f^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\mathbf G_{m,D}$, restricting to the canonical map on $\mu_{\ell^n}$. These maps give a morphism from the inverse image of the Kummer sequence on $C$ to the Kummer sequence on $D$: inclusion commutes, and $c_f(u^{\ell^n})=c_f(u)^{\ell^n}$. The sequences are short exact by [lem-sc-kummer-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] first to the inverse-image sequence and then coefficient naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] to this comparison morphism. The result is $f^*\delta_{C,n}(L)=\delta_{D,n}(f^*L)$, where [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic-pullback] identifies the induced map on $H^1(\mathbf G_m)$ with pullback of invertible modules. These statements apply to arbitrary scheme morphisms between the curves; no $k$-linearity of $f$ is required.

source.place: Section 01FT, delta-functor naturality; etale-cohomology.tex Section 04I0, functoriality; Tag 040E for the Picard identification

proof.text: If $P$ is a closed point of $C$, the isomorphism $f$ has a unique closed inverse image $Q$. Its isomorphism of local rings preserves normalized valuations: for a nonzero regular element $h$ and $j\geq0$, the condition $v_P(h)\geq j$ is membership in the $j$th power of the maximal ideal. The local-ring isomorphism preserves these powers, hence valuations on regular elements and then on rational functions by taking quotients. Applying the valuation-bounded description of $\mathcal O(E)$ in [def-sc-divisor] on corresponding opens therefore gives $f^*\mathcal O_C(P)\cong\mathcal O_D(Q)$. Step 6 sends the Kummer point class at $P$ to the Kummer point class at $Q$. Both have trace $1$ by hypothesis. Additivity and the generation proved in Step 1 give $\operatorname{tr}_{D,n}\circ f^*=\operatorname{tr}_{C,n}$. This argument uses the scheme isomorphism and point classes, so it also covers a nontrivial automorphism of the base field.

source.place: Remark 14.6: point class and trace; divisor pullback under a scheme isomorphism checked directly from the valuation definition

proof.text:
The canonical pullback identifications of the constant sheaf and roots-of-unity sheaf preserve evaluation: pullback of units respects $z\mapsto z^a$ for every integer $a$, and pullback of a constant integer residue class is that same residue class. Apply [lem-wf-etale-cup-functoriality] with the three canonical coefficient maps along $f$. It gives
$$f^*(x\smile y)=f^*x\smile f^*y.$$
The lemma is about small etale sites and arbitrary scheme morphisms; the coefficient square just checked therefore also applies to this semilinear scheme isomorphism.

For $i=0,1,2$, the degrees $i$ and $2-i$ are nonnegative. Apply $\operatorname{tr}_{C,m}$ to the cup equality of Step 5 and use Step 4 to obtain $P^i_{C,m}(r_{n,m}x,s_{n,m}y)=\rho(P^i_{C,n}(x,y))$. Apply $\operatorname{tr}_{D,n}$ to Step 8 and use Step 7 to obtain $P^i_{D,n}(f^*x,f^*y)=P^i_{C,n}(x,y)$. These are the two asserted equalities.

source.place: Theorem 14.7, Example 14.8 and section 22: the trace-cup pairing; assembly of the preceding naturality identities

The ordinary small-etale abelian-sheaf category is Grothendieck; this verifies the enough-injectives hypothesis in the generic connecting-map argument.
